=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27362-27366 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `already_released` check in `release_head_bound_needs_human_latches` accepts the release marker from any commenter, with no trusted-author predicate.
  WHY: Any commenter can post the public marker for the current head, so the poller skips the auto-release with `already_released` and the latch stays until the head moves. Severity disagreement: NIT (sonnet, glm) vs MAJOR (gemini, minimax, openai).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27237 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The header comment names `NEEDS_HUMAN_HEAD_LATCH_BIND_MINUTES (30)` as if it were configurable, but the code hard-codes `local hl_bind_minutes=30`.
  WHY: An operator who sets the variable gets no effect, and the comment introduces a nonexistent identifier (§10).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27283-27370 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Every `ai:needs-human` PR costs paginated comments, events and `pulls/<n>` reads on every tick, with no cache, before the cheap `head_unchanged` skip.
  WHY: This consumes the shared GH_PAT rate-limit budget (§14), and the `pulls` read plus `head_unchanged` check could move ahead of the events read. Severity disagreement: NIT (sonnet, minimax, glm) vs MAJOR (gemini).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27330-27367 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The function decides on earlier comment and event snapshots, then deletes `ai:needs-human` without revalidating the newest latch comment or label event. The sibling `release_staged_support_needs_human_latches` does revalidate before its write.
  WHY: A fresh latch written between the reads and the DELETE is removed while `outcome=released` is logged. Severity disagreement: NIT (sonnet) vs MAJOR (minimax, openai, glm).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27360-27375 (call sites 30845 and 37987) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The two unsynchronized call sites can overlap across concurrent runs, causing duplicate release comments or a 404 on the second DELETE logged as `label_write_failed`.
  WHY: The effect is redundant API calls and log noise, and the release itself stays correct.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27367-27383 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The label is deleted before the explanation comment is posted, so a failed comment POST leaves no audit comment and no retry (`released_comment_failed`).
  WHY: The PR no longer matches the listing, so the audit trail is permanently lost. Severity disagreement: MAJOR (minimax) vs NIT (glm, which notes the sibling staged-support release uses the same order).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
(No task gaps reported.)
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:`already_released` check | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The release-once guard accepts a matching release marker from any commenter, with no trusted-author check.
  WHY: An untrusted commenter can make every tick log `already_released`, so the auto-release is denied until the head moves.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:header comment of `release_head_bound_needs_human_latches` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The header names `NEEDS_HUMAN_HEAD_LATCH_BIND_MINUTES (30)`, which no code reads; the window is a hard-coded `hl_bind_minutes=30`.
  WHY: The comment makes the window look configurable and introduces a nonexistent identifier (§10).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:comments read, events read, `pulls/<n>` read and DELETE sequence | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The latch comment and label event are evaluated once, and the fresh `pulls/<n>` read does not confirm they are still the newest.
  WHY: A new latch written within the loop's few seconds could be removed by the unconditional DELETE. The window is narrow and a repeat failure re-latches.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:per-PR loop reads | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Each `ai:needs-human` PR costs 2 to 3 paginated API calls per tick with nothing cached.
  WHY: The load grows with parked PRs times tick frequency, though the saving from reordering is minor.
- HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27362-27364 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `already_released` marker check does not verify that the marker comment's author is trusted.
  WHY: Anyone can post the marker and stop the auto-release from running for that head.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27237 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The header comment references `NEEDS_HUMAN_HEAD_LATCH_BIND_MINUTES (30)` as configurable, but the code hard-codes `local hl_bind_minutes=30`.
  WHY: An operator changing the variable gets no effect.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27283-27370 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The function makes three consecutive GH API calls inside a per-PR loop on every tick.
  WHY: This violates §14, consumes the rate limit and needs a negative cache or batching.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27360-27375 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The two call sites (`:37987` and `:30845`) are not synchronized.
  WHY: Overlapping runs cause redundant API calls and possible 404s on the second DELETE.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27362-27366 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `already_released` check uses an unanchored `contains($m)` with no `author_association` or bot-login filter, and the marker is publicly derivable.
  WHY: A spoofed marker makes every tick log `already_released` and the PR stays latched. The sibling `later_needs_human_comment` check at 27330-27336 already applies the trusted-author predicate.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27237 vs 27270 vs 27323-27327 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The header documents `NEEDS_HUMAN_HEAD_LATCH_BIND_MINUTES (30)`, but the code uses a hard-coded `local hl_bind_minutes=30` with no env lookup.
  WHY: An operator setting the variable gets a silent no-op.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27283-27370 (comments 27290, events 27320, pulls 27336, `head_unchanged` 27348) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `head_unchanged` is checked only after all three reads, and `latch_head_missing` PRs repeat the reads indefinitely with no negative cache.
  WHY: This spends GH_PAT budget on outcomes already known to be negative.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27283-27385 vs 27367 vs 37987 vs 30845 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The function deletes the label without re-validating the latest latch comment or label event. The sibling `release_staged_support_needs_human_latches` has a `latch_changed_during_release` guard.
  WHY: A fresh latch written between the events read and the DELETE is silently destroyed.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:37987 and 30845 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The post-loop block and the `UNBLOCK_SCAN_SWEEP_ONLY` idle-tick block can interleave for the same PR and head.
  WHY: The second DELETE can 404 and log `label_write_failed`, which pollutes logs.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27367 precedes 27378 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The label is deleted before the audit comment is posted, so a failed POST yields `released_comment_failed` and is never retried.
  WHY: The audit comment is permanently lost. The sibling functions and the cap-escalation path post the comment first.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27283-27370 (27290, 27320, 27336) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Each `ai:needs-human` PR costs comments, events and pulls reads before the `head_unchanged` skip, and `latch_head_missing` PRs repeat this indefinitely.
  WHY: Long-parked PRs add hundreds of API reads per day to the shared budget, and the two call sites compound it on idle ticks.
- HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

  PROBLEM: The release-once check accepts a matching marker from any comment author, unlike the latch-comment check at 27295-27308.
  WHY: A commenter can post the public marker, and the poller reports `already_released` and leaves the label in place.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27330-27367 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The function uses earlier comment and event snapshots plus a fresh PR read that checks only head and labels, then deletes `ai:needs-human` without revalidating the latch history.
  WHY: A newer diagnosis comment or label re-add after the snapshots is deleted anyway. The sibling staged-support release revalidates at `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27161-27170`.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27362-27366 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `already_released` guard accepts the marker from any commenter, while the latch comment (27296) and re-assertion check (27325) require a trusted author.
  WHY: A drive-by commenter makes the poller skip with `already_released` on every tick, so the feature degrades to the old human-clear behaviour. This is availability-degrading, not escalation.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27290-27367 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The function decides on comment and event snapshots and deletes the label without re-reading either. The sibling `latch_changed_during_release` guard at 27170 has no equivalent here, although the header comment (27241-27245) claims the fresh read is the guard.
  WHY: A fresh cap or diagnosis comment plus label written before the DELETE is removed, and the release comment describes the wrong latch.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:30845 and 37987 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Across concurrent workflow runs the two call sites can double-release.
  WHY: The second DELETE 404s and logs `label_write_failed`, and a duplicate release comment is posted. The effect is cosmetic.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27367-27383 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The label is removed before the explanation comment, so a failed comment write is never retried.
  WHY: The audit comment is permanently lost. The sibling staged-support release uses the same order.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27290, 27330, 27348 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A PR parked on an unchanged head pays a paginated events read every tick before the `head_unchanged` check.
  WHY: Moving the pulls read and `head_unchanged` check ahead of the events read is behaviour-preserving and saves GH_PAT budget.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27237 vs 27270 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The header comment names `NEEDS_HUMAN_HEAD_LATCH_BIND_MINUTES (30)`, which no code reads; only the hard-coded local at 27270 exists.
  WHY: An operator setting it gets a silent no-op, and the name is an unregistered identifier (§10).
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
